name: Lot’s wife
charge: Looking back toward Sodom against the angel’s command
summary: The angels told them to escape for their lives and not look behind them. Brought out of the city by the hand, his wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt, a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. She looked back because she loved what was burning; for her to look back at all says she had never agreed to leave. Christ made her a proverb in three words: Remember Lot’s wife.
offenseFull: The instruction came with the rescue and it was specific: escape for your life, look not behind you, stay not in all the plain, escape to the mountain, or be consumed (Genesis 19:17). She had already been taken out by the hand together with her husband and her two daughters, the Lord being merciful to them (Genesis 19:16). The city she was leaving was the city whose men, old and young, from every quarter, had compassed her own house to know the two strangers, and had pressed against her own door (Genesis 19:4-7). Yet she looked back from behind him, against the word given to her (Genesis 19:26).

Ask why any woman would look back at that. The place was not a ruin: it was rich, glorious, full of the things the eyes want, and she loved that life. Somebody in that house was not vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked (2 Peter 2:7-8). For her to turn at all says she had never agreed to leave in the first place; she was grieving what was burning. Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world, for all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life, is not of the Father but is of the world, and the world passes away (1 John 2:15-17). The psalm asks who will rise up for the Lord against the evildoers and who will stand up against the workers of iniquity, and she had not (Psalms 94:16).
judgmentFull: She became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). Wisdom keeps that standing pillar as a monument of an unbelieving soul, and the waste land that smokes as a testimony of the wickedness to this day (Wisdom of Solomon 10:6-7). Christ set her among the weightiest words in the scriptures. He said it would be as in the days of Lot, when they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted and builded, until the same day that Lot went out of Sodom and it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all; and so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed, and in that day the man upon the housetop is not to come down for his goods, nor the man in the field to turn back. Remember Lot’s wife (Luke 17:28-32).

Babylon has an end, and whoever wants to carry Babylon into the kingdom is looking back the way she looked back; a man that puts his hand to the plough and looks back is not fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:62). She was not left behind. She was led out by the hand, by angels, ahead of the fire, with the mercy of the Lord upon her, and still she did not make it, because being led out is not the end of obedience.

Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

lawsResolved.text: You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.
No man, having put his hand to the plow (to follow and serve God), and then looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
God is angered at those who turn their heart from Him.

text.text: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.

And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the Lord being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.
And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him,
And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:
(For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)
Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.
And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?
When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.

Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
Remember Lot’s wife.
And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
Remember Lot’s wife.
Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
